experiment: Intended as Trip 5c on MDK2 (audio-track capture). The bench never ran: /KUI/bench.cfg was larger than the runtime's 2048-byte limit and was ignored, so the bench refused. The session then probed the disc and started a NEW capture of MDK2 with the DEFAULT options (SHA-256+CRC32, end read-back on, ui_hz=2), which was stopped during track 1.

disc.title: MDK2
disc.note: FAD 63000, which t5c-capture-audio.cfg ships, IS inside track 4 (52440-74365, audio) on this disc: the disc choice was right.

what_happened: /KUI/bench.cfg is larger than 2048 bytes; ignored (twice), then 'Bench refused'. The only shipped file over that limit is docs/bench.cfg.example at 5347 bytes.
DISC PROBE PASS: both TOCs, 93 samples.
NEW CAPTURE of MDK2 with default options; stopped by the user during track 1 after 32212992 bytes; 'Partial job preserved: /KUI/dumps/df838eac34967ae16-0001'; retries=0.

conclusions: The capture engine ran at 545.4 KiB/s on MDK2's data track 1 with the old defaults at ui_hz=2, against 551.2 KiB/s for the same settings on Sword in Trip 5a (-1.0%): the engine behaves the same on a second disc.

Time split: SD write 48.2%, SHA-256 23.0%, disc 22.0%, CRC32 4.2%, EDC 2.1%. SHA-256 alone is 23.0% here, which is what capture_hash=crc32 removes. (The setup phase's own disc figure of 92.1% is the 93-sample disc probe, a different block.)
Stop-and-checkpoint worked on a 31-track disc: the job was preserved with a committed byte count and no retries. The RESUME half of that test has still not been run.
No audio-track read rate yet: the capture stopped inside data track 1, and the bench that would have measured track 4 never ran.

limitations: A single partial track of one disc, stopped by hand; not a repeatable measurement.
Old capture defaults (SHA-256 + end read-back), not the fast settings.
